rows.context: Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (final pre-launch M+ tier list, ranked for the highest keys)
rows.text: Top of S tier and his pick for best spec in the season: among the highest overall damage while also leading single-target boss damage, and it keeps full priority damage during AoE with some funnel on top. He reads the defensive complaints as outdated — two baseline Barrier charges, a Mirror Image stagger and extra avoidance make it durable enough to build around.

rows.context: Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (final pre-launch M+ tier list, ranked for the highest keys)
rows.text: Second S-tier spec, which he flags as a surprise. Lower overall than the big AoE specs but single-target priority damage on par with Arcane, and unusually strong on two-to-three target cleave, which he says several dungeons in the pool reward for long stretches. Caveat: it is on Slayer now, which he rates weaker than Colossus. He expects nearly every comp to run Arcane or Arms, often both.

rows.context: Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (final pre-launch M+ tier list, ranked for the highest keys)
rows.text: Top of A+. Strong damage with two builds — Annihilator for AoE with low single target, Voidguard for single target with moderate AoE — plus Chaos Brand, Darkness and genuine tankiness, which he argues is undervalued after watching DK/DH survive content others could not in Season 1. He calls it the most likely spec to round out a group; the caveats are having to commit to one build and very high sims that could invite a raid-driven nerf.

rows.context: Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (final pre-launch M+ tier list, ranked for the highest keys)
rows.text: A tier. Very good sustained five-target damage, now a consistent rather than bursty spec, decent single target and workable two-to-three target on the Farseer build, plus Skyfury as a group buff. Held out of S only because he thinks several comparable specs exist, and because stacking it with other squishy specs worries him defensively. He notes all mail specs are roughly 3% inflated on PTR by a mail-only bug.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ healer tier list
rows.text: Jak's only S-tier healer. He credits the raw output: the tier set turns Holy Light into an Infusion of Light engine (Inflorescence granting two, Judgment a 20% chance) and the 2-set doubles the healing of those Infusion-empowered Flash of Lights, while Virtue spell-queuing and Shield of the Righteous keep mana workable. He notes the post-buff Holy Shock means it is no longer a no-Shock build, and that the poison-dispel-heavy dungeon pool (six of eight) plus bleeds make Cleanse Toxins and Blessing of Protection unusually valuable. His own caveat: no raid buff and low personal damage, so if another healer is tuned to comparable output while bringing Skyfury or Mark of the Wild, Paladin can fall off the list.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ healer tier list
rows.text: A tier, and the top of it. Despite the Farseer buffs he still finds Totemic better in most dungeons — Farseer's single-target healing is good but the niche rarely gets realised when AoE healing is what the pull demands. He likes the tier set's extra Healing Rains stacking with Downpour and Acid Rain, especially in melee comps where everyone is inside them, but rates the raw output clearly below Holy Paladin (good AoE, weak single target) and calls the gameplay unexciting with no new resource or Apex interaction. Skyfury and Poison Cleansing Totem are what keep it high.

rows.reason: No unambiguous absolute placement preserved in this video paraphrase
rows.context: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ healer tier list
rows.text: He argues the attempt to force mastery into a good position broke the spec: buffing mastery while nerfing the Forecaster-side caster healing made the Rising Sun Kick / Ancient Teachings build dominant, and then the ~60% Morning Breeze cut removed it without restoring the rest. Conduit and Revival no longer feel like real cooldowns; Chi-Ji and Thunder Focus Tea still work but are much weaker; and the Season 1 backstop of falling back on casted healing does not function any more. His conclusion is blunt for a spec that was recently top of the list: Mistweaver actually needs buffs to get back to a good position.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ healer tier list
rows.text: B tier. Output with the Oracle setup is fine — permanent Shadow Mend access, Surge of Light discounts and Divine Aegis absorbs off crits make it reliable — but Voidweaver is too weak, and the season's biggest problem is the dispel profile: with poisons in six of eight dungeons, a group that cannot cover the dispels eats through Pain Suppression charges. Mana is better than Season 1 but still has no active regeneration (even Shadowfiend barely helps), so drinking stops are unavoidable.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ healer tier list
rows.text: C tier. He rates Oracle considerably stronger than Archon right now and says the healing output itself is genuinely good, but the spec is dragged down by cooldowns that do not feel strong (Prayer of Healing goes on the back burner without Archon's modifiers), heavy immobility, and weak Prayer of Mending. The revamped Apex turning every Serenity into a Benediction Flash Heal helps single-target but leaves it with no tool to lift the whole party at once. He credits a real niche — one of the strongest healers into rot damage — while concluding other healers are simply too well-rounded to pass up.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ healer tier list
rows.text: C tier, and his harshest read of the list. He accepts the Tranquility quality-of-life change but says everything else made the spec worse: losing the Swiftmend HoT extension and Burden of Vision leaves the HoTs feeling inert, the shift onto Clearcasting Regrowth does not compensate, and the granular control that made Resto Druid satisfying in dungeons is gone. Mastery no longer feels powerful, and outside Convoke or a trinket he does not see the output meeting the season's heal checks. He notes he has never seen Druid players this unhappy with the spec, and quotes one on stream to that effect.

rows.reason: No unambiguous absolute placement preserved in this video paraphrase
rows.context: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ healer tier list
rows.text: He rates the healing side as fully covered — the 2-set fires a Living Flame on Essence Burst consumption, the 4-set guarantees Essence Burst off Verdant Embrace, and Flame Shaper is strong with Dream Breath HoTs plus Fluttering Seedlings triggering Consume Flame — and he is seeing 90-100k personal damage in dungeons off double Fire Breath charges. What drags it down the list is unchanged: a proactive setup cost, far more GCDs and cognitive load than other healers, and an almost non-existent raid cooldown. His framing is that Preservation mains can meet the hardest HPS checks, but the extra work buys no extra reward over an easier healer.

rows.reason: No unambiguous absolute placement preserved in this video paraphrase
rows.context: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 RAID healer tier list (Dummy Dome group testing)
rows.text: His top healer for Season 2 raid. Disc puts out huge healing AND roughly 70k+ single-target damage through progression, which he calls enormously helpful for a race-to-world-first environment, and he notes there is no penalty for stacking two of them (Power Infusion on top). Mana is fantastic, especially on Voidweaver. He airs Klanden's caveat with it: numbers and damage are good — arguably too high — but Voidweaver play style is "ignore your Disc fundamentals and press good buttons on cooldown", Oracle is falling behind, and heavy movement hurts because Void Blast cannot be cast while moving.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 RAID healer tier list (Dummy Dome group testing)
rows.text: A tier. Pres "blasted tons of healing" in the testing, with the Flameshaper setup putting better emphasis on Dream Breath and Consume Flame working with both fluttering seedlings and Verdant Embrace. It looked best when the raid was hard-stacked but still did a fantastic job on a light spread, and its mana economy read as being in a good spot. He cites UT's hands-on impression of being flooded with Essence Burst procs and going well over a million HPS inside a Stasis window.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 RAID healer tier list (Dummy Dome group testing)
rows.text: A tier. He argues an underrated effect of the PTR's ~30% health-pool inflation is that Holy Light and Lay on Hands are no longer overweight, so the whole kit is appropriately sized to the new health bars. Output was "incredibly, incredibly high", especially on-demand spot healing. Caveat from Clarius after testing: it feels really strong when overhealing is low, hard to get value out of Virtue when other healers snipe it, and mana is a bit tight (though that should ease on a real fight where Virtue is not pressed on cooldown). He is unsure which Paladin spec ends up the race-to-world-first pick.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 RAID healer tier list (Dummy Dome group testing)
rows.text: B tier and the only spec there — he calls Resto Shaman the dark horse, "a tier away" from the world-first conversation. Strong when the raid can stack, and he flags Coiled Altar as a fight that should suit it (pulsing AoE plus stacking healing absorbs). The blocker is comp value rather than throughput: Harik's read, which he endorses, is that the numbers are genuinely good and mana is workable, but there is no reason to bring a Shaman as the fourth healer over a second Disc Priest unless you specifically want the Skyfury buff. One healer nerf above it would move it.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 RAID healer tier list (Dummy Dome group testing)
rows.text: C tier. He tried both Oracle and Archon and says Holy Priest simply needs its passive healing to be stronger to succeed. Oracle should be favoured by a raid full of ticking rot damage and Prompt Prophecy buffs, but it was not — Archon was still stronger and is enormously bursty (Halo plus Apotheosis smashes health bars), while the gaps between cooldowns are boring and mana-starved. Every single test run ended near or at zero mana. His diagnosis: Blizzard keeps cutting Flash Heal and Prayer of Healing mana costs while removing the free casts (Surge of Light, Apotheosis Holy Words), so full-price casting still drains the bar.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 RAID healer tier list (Dummy Dome group testing)
rows.text: C tier. Meg tested mastery-heavy Ancient Teachings and caster Mistweaver variants across multiple cooldown and comp setups and Mistweaver struggled throughout — not out of mana, but not producing much healing either. Her read, which he presents: the caster spells do nothing, the 8% aura nerf was unneeded given the state of the other healers, and Ancient Teachings only looks better because it is damage-based and therefore untouched by the healing-aura nerf. Her conclusion is that you would not bring a Monk in any competitive situation right now.

rows.reason: No unambiguous absolute placement preserved in this video paraphrase
rows.context: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 RAID healer tier list (Dummy Dome group testing)
rows.text: Bottom of the list. He says Resto Druid has been struggling through all of Season 2 PTR testing and that the quality-of-life additions have left the spec feeling worse overall. Even in the environment that should suit it — stacked raid, constant rot and ticking damage — it consistently landed at the bottom of the group's raw output, with the testing splitting into a clear winners group and losers group. Viteman's asks, which he relays: buff HoTs, rework the 4-piece (the old one that granted Clearcasting synergised better), and rebuff Regrowth.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — final pre-launch Season 2 Mythic+ spec tier list update
rows.text: He keeps Blood in S+ and reads it as both the tankiest tank and the highest-damage one, explicitly noting the placement survives the most recent nerf. He later describes tanking as an island — every other tank sits a tier lower missing either damage or survivability — and builds all three of his suggested meta comps around Blood.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — final pre-launch Season 2 Mythic+ spec tier list update
rows.text: He keeps Holy Paladin in S+ as the best healer at keeping a group alive. He names two real costs — weak healer damage and no raid buff — but resolves them in the spec's favour on the grounds that survival is what a healer is for. He stays unconvinced by the Preservation Evoker case that is pulling other people's lists, saying he wants to see it heal high keys consistently first.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — final pre-launch Season 2 Mythic+ spec tier list update
rows.text: He calls Arms probably the best DPS in the game right now, or at least the best melee, and keeps it in S+. His reasons are the combination he considers decisive for this season: good funnel, good priority damage and good target swapping, plus a lot of AoE and stops, on a spec that can make itself tanky with Spell Reflection and Defensive Stance when needed.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — final pre-launch Season 2 Mythic+ spec tier list update
rows.text: Of the non-Blood tanks he says Protection Warrior is missing the most, and his reasoning is that it has been conditional since Dragonflight: it is only good where Spell Reflection is good. He gives Ruby Life Pools as the dungeon where that pays off and says it is completely useless in some others, landing it at the bottom of his A- tank group.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — final pre-launch Season 2 Mythic+ spec tier list update
rows.text: He puts every Druid spec in A and says they are not good enough that he would bring one even after counting Mark of the Wild and Stampeding Roar. On Guardian specifically he reads it as tanky enough but short on damage if built for survivability. He adds the flip side: because the buff floor for a Mark of the Wild carrier is lower, one buff to Guardian or one nerf to Blood would put it back into his fizz comp.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — final pre-launch Season 2 Mythic+ spec tier list update
rows.text: He drops Retribution to B and reads it as significantly worse than last season, naming a few bosses that make it bad to play. His comparative point is that it competes for the same non-buff-carrying damage slot as the Rogue specs, and he considers Rogue far better this season.

cohorts.label: LBNinja7
cohorts.creator: LBNinja7
cohorts.scopeNote: A named dated video panel preserved as attributed paraphrases; later revisions remain separately dated.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — S2 M+ healer tier list (corrected)
rows.text: Corrects his earlier ranking and drops Mistweaver a clear step below Holy Paladin, to the back of A tier. As a Mistweaver main he says the Rising Sun Kick nerf hurts less on its own than people expected — the globals still heal well for their cost — but that it exposed how little Shaluun's Gift and the spec's spot healing contribute now they are no longer hidden behind the oversized kicks. Calls it a jack of all trades, master of none, and says he has not enjoyed its PTR raid healing outside Chi-Ji.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — S2 M+ healer tier list (corrected)
rows.text: Ranks Holy Paladin the best healer and the lone S tier, though deliberately not S+, on survivability and large burst healing. His one reservation is composition: it brings Devotion Aura but does not amplify the Blood DK / Arcane Mage / Warrior core he says has been dominating PTR keys, the way Mistweaver or Resto Shaman can — which he thinks leaves a window open for those two in push groups.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — S2 M+ healer tier list (corrected)
rows.text: Moves Resto Shaman to the top of A tier as the consistent healer of the season and expects it to chisel its way into the meta composition — helped, he notes, by its raid buff being unlikely to be covered by a DPS spec in the group.

rows.reason: No unambiguous absolute placement preserved in this video paraphrase
rows.context: 12.1 PTR — S2 M+ healer tier list (corrected)
rows.text: Keeps Discipline in the solid middle — 'still very solid' — below the top three but comfortably clear of the bottom, and in comp terms he treats it as the better of the two Priest healers rather than the other way round.

rows.reason: No unambiguous absolute placement preserved in this video paraphrase
rows.context: 12.1 PTR — S2 M+ healer tier list (corrected)
rows.text: Continues to call Preservation the healer people are not looking at — still very solid and his standing sleeper pick for the season.

rows.reason: No unambiguous absolute placement preserved in this video paraphrase
rows.context: 12.1 PTR — S2 M+ healer tier list (corrected)
rows.text: Defends Holy Priest as better than its reputation — he notes the recent healing buff and says it has climbed steadily from a genuinely bad early PTR — but keeps it near the bottom because of comp: he reads it as essentially a worse Disc Priest in a group.

rows.reason: No unambiguous absolute placement preserved in this video paraphrase
rows.context: 12.1 PTR — S2 M+ healer tier list (corrected)
rows.text: Same shape as his Holy Priest read: much improved since early PTR and better than a lot of people think, but he reads it as a worse Resto Shaman in a composition, which caps where it can land. Stresses the whole list is PTR speculation and should be taken with a grain of salt.

cohorts.label: MadSkillzzTV
cohorts.creator: MadSkillzzTV
cohorts.scopeNote: A named dated video panel preserved as attributed paraphrases; later revisions remain separately dated.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ testing
rows.text: Drops Mistweaver to A tier in his retested M+ list. The mastery-stacking Morning Breeze / Rising Sun Kick build he had been calling S+ (Mistweavers doing 90–100k damage in keys with the healing to match) is dead after Morning Breeze effectiveness was cut 60%, on top of the ~8% overall healing nerf. Back on a normal stat priority it still felt quite strong on both damage and healing, but he calls the Sheilun/Vivify part of the toolkit weak and expects Blizzard to revisit it — which is why he no longer puts it in S.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ testing
rows.text: His biggest riser: high A tier, and he says some people would put it in S. Holy Shock healing +50% and its cheaper mana finally killed the no-Holy-Shock build, and the 4-set now carries what he thinks may be the first outright negative tier-set clause (Holy Light mana cost +60% in the notes, closer to 50% datamined) offset by a 5% healing increase. He reads that trade as good: you save Holy Light for emergencies and always have a button, and the spec's gameplay is simply better for it. Lightsmith with Beacon of Virtue pleasantly surprised him and he thinks he had been sleeping on it. Stays A only out of cautious optimism.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ testing
rows.text: Keeps Resto Shaman where it was (A tier) and says he could nitpick it into S. He is explicitly happy about the tier-set nerf: the spec has too much of its power sitting in RNG (tier set, Ascendance and Stormstream procs), so moving power out of the set and into the baseline toolkit is the right direction. Farseer's Chain Heal buffs made that tree feel decent, but Totemic in a full physical-melee composition felt really great, and he would be surprised if Totemic Resto is not part of that comp in Season 2.

rows.reason: No unambiguous absolute placement preserved in this video paraphrase
rows.context: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ testing
rows.text: Calls Preservation the biggest underdog and most underappreciated healer on the PTR — healing is there, damage is absolutely there, and he likes the tier set (mostly tested Flame Shaper, plus an Emerald Blossom / Fluttering Seedlings build). But he separates that from the meta question and answers it himself: probably not meta, because it is harder to pilot, has range limitations and no good raid buff. Held at its existing placement.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ testing
rows.text: The healer that falls in this update — down to a new B+ row, because he admits he was generous in last week's ranking before testing most of the builds. A week focused on Oracle left mana still an issue and, more importantly, he wants more Atonement transfer in the panic moments: every healer above Discipline gave him an easier time in the same keys. He thinks a couple more tuning passes could make it climb, and that Blizzard is nervous about tuning it for M+ without breaking raid.

rows.reason: No unambiguous absolute placement preserved in this video paraphrase
rows.context: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ testing
rows.text: Held in place. The Abundance / Regrowth buffs and the Abundance crit bug fix landed, but he still wants further M+ buffs, and calls Wildstalker Resto's damage quite low — partly because there is no time to apply bleeds when the healing demand is that high. He also misses Verdant Infusion no longer extending HoTs and says he is jealous of the HoT-extension talent Resto Shaman just got. Expects Blizzard to keep buffing it, but flags that as speculation.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ testing
rows.text: Stays around B tier. He is clear that Holy Priest is not bad and can push decently high keys, and the Oracle buffs (Premonition of Insight, Prayer of Mending) landed, but the currently popular dual-Oracle build leaves him with few healing buttons for his taste, its damage sits on the low end, and he wants significant — including gameplay — changes he is not holding his breath for.

cohorts.label: Kalamazi
cohorts.creator: Kalamazi
cohorts.scopeNote: A named dated video panel preserved as attributed paraphrases; later revisions remain separately dated.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ build dummy testing
rows.text: Kalamazi's own M+-build dummy tests put Demonology ahead of the other two locks: roughly 130k sustained single target versus Affliction's ~110k, with near-identical baseline AoE (~380k) that climbs to 410-420k in Tyrant/implosion windows — the biggest cooldown swing of the three. He says the 20% Diabolist pet nerf still left the spec's Ruination, big-imp and axe-demon damage intact, and that "demo's not OP, it's just like aff is that bad". His ranking for 12.1 Mythic+ if it launched today: Demonology, then Affliction, then Destruction.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ build dummy testing
rows.text: Kalamazi measures Affliction's M+-build single target at ~110k and calls the sustain outside cooldowns "abysmal … diabolically bad", pinning it on Unstable Affliction being undertuned — he wants roughly a 30% UA buff, which would also lift the tier set since it scales off baseline UA. AoE holds up at ~380k on Seed spam, and he credits the apex-talent and Dark Harvest bug fixes for a small AoE gain, but the Nocturnal Yield removal means Nightfall procs no longer give free instant Seeds, so shard economy and Agony upkeep now genuinely constrain the rotation. He ranks it second of the three for keys and says a UA buff is all it needs to be the pick.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ build dummy testing
rows.text: Kalamazi still calls Destruction "our highest tuned spec currently in single target" — about 120k in his M+-build test, and steady rather than spiky — but adds that all three lock specs are subpar in single target versus other classes. In AoE it lands around 360-370k and is the hardest of the three to actually reach, because Mayhem keeps proccing on the main target or on low-health mobs; he says players have asked for two years to have Mayhem skip the primary target. He ranks it third of the three for 12.1 Mythic+ and describes the gameplay as sustaining one number rather than anything engaging.

cohorts.label: Bansherz
cohorts.creator: Bansherz
cohorts.scopeNote: A named dated video panel preserved as attributed paraphrases; later revisions remain separately dated.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 key testing stream; answering directly on where Hunter lands in keys
rows.text: Asked to rank Marksmanship, he puts it at roughly B tier and says he would place all three Hunter specs around B. His framing is that Hunter is solid and in a pretty good spot but simply not meta — his advice is that a Hunter main or one-trick will be completely fine, while someone chasing the best spec in the game should not swap to Hunter. He also says that with no Hunter spec overtuned the right approach is to flex between at least the two ranged specs rather than commit to one, and he confirms he is staying on Hunter himself. He caveats that a buff could land any day and change the placement.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 key testing stream; answering directly on where Hunter lands in keys
rows.text: He groups Beast Mastery with the rest of the class at around B tier for keys — solid, in a pretty good spot, but not meta. The same advice follows: fine for a Hunter main, not the pick for someone chasing the strongest spec, and worth flexing between the ranged specs rather than committing. He flags that tuning could still move it.

rows.context: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 key testing stream; answering directly on where Hunter lands in keys
rows.text: Within a class he places around B tier for keys, he singles out Survival as probably the highest of the three — higher B tier — while keeping it inside the same 'solid but not meta' band as Marksmanship and Beast Mastery. He adds the same caveat that Hunter could be buffed at any point before launch.

scales._comment: Tier-scale definitions and the normalization map. Each source declares which scale it uses (sources.json → scale). Values place every tier on one 0–100 axis so sources with different scales can be averaged into a consensus. Consensus bands must be sorted by descending min, ending at 0. 2026-08-14 (owner decision, Riley — applied ahead of the 08-18 flip rather than in the flip commit): the LIVE icyveins scale is now the SAME seven bands as icyveins-ptr. Icy Veins rebuilt its live M+ lists for Midnight Season 2 and they publish S+ and B+, which the old five-band scale could not represent — the merge had been blocked for six days because storing an S+ letter would have failed validation and collapsing it into S was refused as fabrication. The two scales are now identical by intent, not coincidence, so the note below about them deliberately diverging is HISTORY: it described the window when only the PTR list had the extra rungs. Measured on landing: re-spacing S from 100 to 92 re-scores the frozen Season-1 letters the consensus still reads through the frozen lane, moving 13 consensus scores and 3 M+ letters (Unholy DK, Devourer DH, Augmentation Evoker, all S -> A+) — a scale decision, not spec movement, which is why CONSENSUS_VERSION went 3 -> 4 in the same commit. Its shared tiers keep the live anchors exactly (A+ 82 / A 66 / B 48 / C 30) so the same author's live and PTR reads are directly comparable on the axis; B+ sits at 57, the midpoint of A and B. 2026-08-04 (owner decision, Riley): the PTR DPS list added a SEVENTH band, S+, in its 02 Aug. "Update #4" — S+ takes the 100 anchor and S shifts down to 92. This is the one place the PTR scale deliberately stops matching the live one: PTR S is 92 while live S is 100, because the PTR list now reserves a rung above S that the live list has no equivalent for. Collapsing S+ into S was rejected — it would fabricate a placement the source is explicitly distinguishing. Note this re-spacing moves every icyveins-ptr-derived projection input, not just the two S+ specs, since the source feeds projectionFor via ptrTierRead at weight .25 (it is era:ptr, so consensus is untouched).

sources.name: Archon
sources.author: Archon.gg (statistical)
sources.methodology: Statistical tier lists computed from Warcraft Logs parses and Blizzard leaderboards — 14-day rolling window, refreshed daily. Raid tiers read from the throughput metric tier list (NOT the default popularity grouping); M+ tiers from the M+ score tier list. EARLY-S2 BASIS (owner decision 2026-08-25): the raid letters come from the HEROIC throughput list while Mythic is sparse — Heroic carries ~170x the parses and covers all 27 DPS specs where Mythic held 6 specs under 10 parses and no Fire Mage at all. Switch back to the Mythic list (a reviewed registry edit + CONSENSUS_VERSION bump) once Mythic reaches 27/27 DPS with healthy samples. The Mythic rankings pages stay registered as ancillary metric feeds. Mirrored at u.gg/wow.
sources.notes: Fetch recipe: parse the __NEXT_DATA__ JSON script tag from raw HTML (WebFetch markdown drops it). Raid pages carry three tierLists (popularity/throughput/survivability) — use metric "throughput"; M+ pages use metric "score". The Heroic raid pages (the letter basis since 2026-08-25) parse with the IDENTICAL recipe — only the /heroic/ path segment differs; the ancillary Mythic rankings pages feed the "(Mythic)" numeric families and survivability. Mirrored at u.gg/wow.
sources.summary: Letter grades computed from logged play. Raid tiers come from its THROUGHPUT list and M+ tiers from its SCORE list — never the default popularity grouping, which ranks how often a spec is played rather than how it performs.
